post.caption: Beethoven's royal ring wasn't diamond. Beethoven's Ninth Symphony premiered in Vienna on May 7, 1824. He was nearly deaf, but he still supervised the premiere. He did not notice the applause until a singer turned him around. In 1826, he dedicated the printed score to Prussia's king. The king wrote to thank him for the symphony. He added that he would send a diamond ring. What arrived was a far cheaper ring with a reddish gem. Beethoven was disappointed, and he sold the ring right away. The ring brought him 300 florins in Vienna currency.
